name: GePETO
description: The GePETO project is a germanium refining recycling project in Belgium. It aims at strengthening Umicore's capabilities through technology development and facility upgrading. This will result in higher germanium recovery yields from existing feed, in innovative processes supporting the recovery of germanium out of complex waste streams from European industry and a more resilient supply of germanium products to the EU value chain.

name: ReGAIN
description: The ReGAlN project is a substitution project, focusing on the expansion and transformation of Umicore's Ge wafering facility located in Olen, Belgium. This project entails the industrialization of a new technology supporting the re-use of germanium substrates. These thin film germanium substrates are serving the space solar cell and industry. These innovative micro-electronics substrates allow the industry to significantly reduce its consumption of germanium, enabling the required growth of the end markets like space power.

name: Chvaletice manganese Project
description: The Chvaletice Manganese Project is an integrated extraction and processing project located in the Czech Republic. The project involves the development of a tailings extraction section and a high-purity refining section to re-process a readily leachable manganese deposit hosted in the tailings of a decommissioned mine. The project's goal is to produce battery grade high-purity manganese products, principally for use in the cathode of lithium-ion batteries in the EU market.

name: Cínovec lithium project
description: Cinovec lithium project is an integrated extraction and processing project located approximately 105 km north-west of Prague, in the historical CinovecZinnwald mining district (Czech Republic). The project aims to extract Zinnwaldite - a lithium bearing mineral - from an underground mine, concentrate the lithium ore and produce battery grade lithium carbonate via chemical processing. The project plans to use renewable energy (solar) for its energy intensive operations.

name: CO2 Graphite
description: C02GRAPHlTE project is a processing project located in Estonia. It aims to build a large-scale facility to produce battery-grade graphite based on the synthesis of carbon materials from carbon dioxide (C02). This technology is the result of R&D efforts started over 10 years ago in the University of Tartu (Estonia).

name: Sakatti Project
description: The Sakatti project by Anglo American is an innovative mining project in northern Finland focused on extracting high-grade strategic raw materials including copper, nickel, platinum group metals and cobalt. Sakatti is being designed and developed as a highly automated, low-carbon underground operation, with minimal surface footprint while providing a secure and stable source of strategic raw materials crucial for the energy and digital transitions. Sakatti expected to deliver around 100,000 tonnes of copperequivalent metal, enough for 1.3 million electric vehicles.

name: KELIBER LITHIUM PROJECT
description: Sibanye-Stillwater's Keliber Lithium Project is a project for integrated lithium extraction and processing in Finland. It aims to develop a sustainable operation to produce battery-grade lithium hydroxide (LiOH). The mining operations and the processing plant are located in Kaustinen and Kokkola, in Central Ostrobothnia, Finland, which holds some of the most significant lithium deposits in Europe. The production process is composed of three stages: mining and production of an ore concentrate in the Kaustinen area, and LiOH production at the refinery in the Kokkola Industrial Park.

name: Kolmisoppi
description: The Kolmisoppi extraction project by Terrafame Ltd in Finland, targeting the exploitation of its substantial nickel and cobalt resources starting in 2028. This initiative aims to extend Terrafame's nickel and cobalt operational capabilities and supporting its integrated battery chemicals plant. The Kolmisoppi project is set to sustain and enhance the production of strategic materials utilizing bioleaching technology that reduces energy consumption and carbon emissions.

name: Project Fortum Hydromet
description: Project Fortum Hydromet is a black mass recycling project in Finland. The project is a planned extension of an existing hydrometallurgical plant producing nickel, cobalt, lithium (battery grade) and copper. The company aims to have the first stage of the expansion operational by 2029, and the fullsized plant is estimated to start in 2032. The new plant is planned to be built in the adjacent land area of the existing plant. The plant will use black mass and pCAM/CAM production waste as its feedstock.

name: Hycamite TCD Technologies Ltd
description: The Hycamite TCD Technologies project is a processing project in Kokkola, Finland. It produces clean hydrogen and solid, high-value carbon products by splitting methane. Through its proprietary catalysts, Hycamite can tailor its carbon products according to customer requirements into, e.g., battery-grade graphite." It is at the construction stage of an industrial-scale demonstration plant at the Kokkola Industrial Park for producing battery-grade graphite using an innovative methane-splitting technology. The project promoter has been operating a pilot plant for approximately 3 years and is further de-risking the process through the construction of a commercial demonstration plant.

name: Jervois Finland Cobalt Refinery Expansion Project
description: The Jervois Finland Cobalt is a processing project in the Kokkola Industrial Park in Finland. It aims to establish a new, state-of-the-art cobalt refinery to produce battery grade cobalt sulphate. The project promoter has deep technological expertise specific to cobalt refining, having manufactured advanced cobalt products at its cobalt refinery facility in Kokkola since 1968. The refinery will leverage existing infrastructure at the Kokkola Industrial Park, which provides necessary utilities and sbpports streamlined operations, contributing to its technical readiness.

name: CAREMAG
description: CAREMAG is a processing project located in France. It aims at creating an environmentally friendly production unit for pure rare earth oxides (Neodymium, Praseodymium, Terbium, Dysprosium) from permanent magnets to be recycled from production scrap (magnet manufacturing, turbine and motor assembly plants) and end-of-life equipment as well as from rareearth concentrates from mines. The processing plant will be built in an existing industrial area, limiting the potential negative environmental impacts. It will make use of the best available technologies for a reduced environmental impact in terms of C02, water use and energy consumption.

name: Emili
description: EMILI is an integrated hard-rock lithium extraction and processing project located in France. The upstream project encompasses an underground mine and a concentration plant to produce a mica concentrate from Beauvoir deposit 40 km away, the EMILI project also aims at constructing a lithium refinery, able to produce battery grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM) using mica ore concentrate as the source of lithium. The project, which will benefit from an operating quarry activity and an existing industrial area, will adhere to IRMA international certification scheme, focusing on minimising environmental impact, maximising resource efficiency and social impact

name: BAM4EVER (Phase I&II)
description: The BAM4EVER project is a processing project located in France. It aims to establish a graphite Battery Anode Material (BAM) production facility to supply European battery gigafactories. The equipment needed for all steps of production is already in place and currently producing at smaller scale. Tokai COBEX Savoie, French subsidiary of a Japanese company is developing an expansion project for industrialising high-performance artificial Graphite BAM that will be 20 times less C02 intensive compared to existing producers and technologies.

name: MagFactory
description: The MagFactory project is a recycling project In France. It aims to establish a cutting-edge production facility for rare earth magnets in Europe. Vertically integrated, the project utilizes a costeffective circular model, from recycling magnet scraps to re-manufacturing new rare earths permanent magnets. The processes involved have been developed by R&D and have been tested at the laboratory and pilot plant levels by the promoters.

name: GALLICAM
description: Sibanye-Stillwater's GalliCam project is a processing project near Le Havre in France. It aims at reconverting the existing Sandouville nickel refinery capacity to be able to produce precursor of Cathode Active Materials (pCAM) containing nickel, manganese, and cobalt (NMC). The project is based on a disruptive direct pCAM production process using hydrochloric acid as primary refining medium from Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP - produced from mines). The process is designed so that it can also use Black Mass (BM - sourced from end-of-life or scrapped batteries) as a feed. The project will be implemented on the Sandouville brownfield site, eliminating the need for artificialisation of new land and reducing its impact on biodiversity.

name: Hydrometallurgy
description: The HYDRO-BATTERY project aims to develop an innovative, effcient and competitive solution for the recycling of electric vehicle batteries or battery production waste (production scraps and end of life batteries), located in Dunkirk, Hauts-de-France region (France). The technology allows recovery of critical raw materials contained in the black mass from battery pretreatment. These obtained materials such as nickel, cobalt, manganese and lithium are of battery quality and can thus be reintroduced into new battery manufacturing. Based on processes mastered by Orano, this technology is distinguished by its economical use of chemical reagents and electrical equipment exclusively allowing to benefit from a highly decarbonized energy available in France.

name: Ageli
description: Ageli is one of the world's most sustainable integrated lithium extraction and processing project, located in France's Alsace region lead by Eramet, EU leader in lithium production and ÉS, world expert in geothermal energy. It aims to extract lithium from geothermal brine to produce battery-grade lithium carbonate. The promoter's intention is to industrialise a sustainable process that combines geothermal energy and lithium production with a low carbon footprint. As an output, Ageli will contribute to supporting the expansion of the EU battery industry over the long term, as it is a key precursor for Lithium-ion batteries used for electric mobility or stationary storage on mainland Europe.

name: Viridian Lithium
description: The Viridian Lithium project is a lithium processing project located in France. The project will operate primarily as a service company to convert various grades of lithium carbonate to refined batterygrade lithium hydroxide monohydrate. This independent lithium refinery aims to provide for the conversion and purification of lithium salts used as cathode precursors for the manufacturing of lithium-ion batteries for Electric Vehicles (EV).

name: European Initiative for Strategic and Sustainable Graphite Production
description: The project European Initiative for Strategic and Sustainable Graphite Production is developing a processing plant in northern France. The project will utilize natural graphite sourced from Northern Graphite's Okanjande mine in Namibia as the input material, to be transformed into high-purity graphite concentrate into battery anode material ("BAM").

name: Zero Carbon Lithium
description: Vulcan is building the world's first carbon neutral, integrated lithium and renewable energy business to decarbonise battery production. Vulcan's Lionheart Project, located in the Upper Rhine Valley Brine Field bordering Germany and France, is the largest lithium resource in Europe and a tier-one lithium project globally. Harnessing natural heat to produce lithium from sub-surface brines and to power conversion to battery-quality material and using its in-house industry-leading Adsorption-Type Direct Lithium Extraction technology VULSORB@, Vulcan is building a local, low-cost source of sustainable lithium for European electric vehicle batteries.

name: ProHiPerSi
description: ProHiPerSi is a substitution project in Germany. It addresses the increase in performance of lithiumion batteries while at the same time reducing the specific production costs through a novel siliconbased anode active material (AAM). The material has been proven to significantly increase both the energy density and the fast-charge capability of state-of-the-art lithium-ion batteries. The AAM has been designed in a way that allows for its gradual implementation into already existing cell production lines as a replacement for graphite.

name: Lithium Hydroxide Converter Guben
description: The Lithium Hydroxide Converter Guben processing project by Rock Tech Guben GmbH is set to develop a conversion plant in Guben, Germany designed to process the lithium bearing ore spodumene into high-quality, battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM) to serve the European markets. Apart from processing primary lithium, the plant will also refine lithium recyclates from recycling, contributing to a closed-loop lithium value chain in the EU.

name: Metlen BAUX-EU, GALLANT, LEADER
description: The BAUX-EU, GALLANT and LEADER projects form an integrated extraction and processing project located in Greece. This project aims to develop an integrated production line for three critical and strategic raw materials in the EU, namely bauxite, gallium and alumina. This project entails an initiative aimed at developing a green extraction line for bauxite, with a main output of alumina, next to additional gallium extraction. Next to this, the project will also develop a new alumina production line, as well as focus on the processing of gallium

name: RECOVER-IT
description: Resources Extraction and Circular Optimization Via Effluent Recovery in Italy RECOVER-IT - is a recycling project in Italy promoted by Circular Materials. It aims to recover strategic raw materials trapped in industrial wastewater through the company's proprietary low carbon intensity SRMs extraction process, including nickel, copper and platinum group metals (PGMs). The Project is already operating from Circular Materials Hub Zero "CMHO" in Cadoneghe (PD) and will reach maximum throughput in Italy by 2029. As capacity for each CMH grows, the company will expand its intake of SRM-rich waste to other sources already successfully tested by the company, including electronic waste and black mass derived from endof-life batteries.

name: Alpha Project
description: Alpha - Recycling project is a recycling project located in Rosignano Solvay (Italy). It aims to establish an in-house palladium (Pd) recovery and catalyst production This initiative is a major step towards 100% circularity for palladium, a critical raw material used for the production of hydrogen peroxide. This project will not only enhance competitiveness and operational efficiency but also contribute to the EU's goal of securing critical raw material supply chains.

name: LIFE-22-ENV- IT- INSPIREE
description: LIFE22-ENV-lT-lNSPlREE is a recycling project in the province of Frosinone, Italy. It aims for the recovery of Rare Earths from NdFeB permanent magnets extracted from hard disks and electric motors. In a two-level process, permanent magnets will first be disassembled (level l), after which REE will be recovered via hydrometallurgy (level II). The output materials of this process will be REE oxides, oxalates, carbonates, and other salts. The Rare Earth Recovery Facility is designed to utilize existing infrastructure of the industrial site.

name: Portovesme CRM Hub
description: The Portovesme CRM Hub is a recycling project in Portovesme, Sardinia, Italy. It aims to use advanced hydrometallurgical technologies to recover critical raw materials from black mass generated by the pre-treatment of end-of-life batteries and scraps sourced across Europe. The facility will convert black mass into Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP) product containing nickel, cobalt and copper, as well as production of lithium carbonate. It strategically bridges the gap by building and operating a black mass treatment facility, using advanced technology with high recoveries rates of critical materials, managing battery chemistry variations and reducing risks and costs.

name: Pulawy Rare Earths Separation Plant
description: T e Pulawy Rare Earths Separation Plant project is set to establish a rare earth elements (REES) separation plant in Pulawy, Poland, dedicated to processing mixed rare earth carbonates into essential oxides such as Neodymium, Praseodymium, and also a heavy rare earth concentrate.

name: POLVOLT
description: POLVOLT is a recycling project in Poland. It focuses on the establishment of a large-scale facility dedicated to the recovery and recycling of critical raw materials crucial for the development of electromobility and renewable energy technologies. Specifically, the facility will focus on the production of chemical compounds of battery metals such as nickel, cobalt, manganese and lithium. The materials will be derived from black mass recovered from spent batteries and production waste from battery manufacturing facilities. The facility will also produce Grade A electrolytic copper, which is vital to produce copper foil used in lithium-ion battery anodes. Platinum Group Metals will be recovered from e-scrap delivered to the plant by extensive Elemental's collection network.

name: Romano Mine
description: The Romano Mine project is a lithium extraction project located in Portugal It aims to mine lithium bearing minerals through both open-pit and underground mining using standard mining technologyq The output of this project would contribute to the production of lithium hydroxide monohydrate, used in both the lithium-ion battery and energy storage industries.

name: Barroso Lithium Project
description: The Barroso Lithium Project is an extraction project located in Northern Portugal. It aims to produce battery grade spodumene concentrate, ceramic feldspar/quartz, and low-grade bulk pegmatite. The project will apply conventional production techniques, amplify positive social impact in the region, while minimising environmental impact, visual disturbance and carbon footprint. The Project Promoter is owned by the listed company, Savannah Resources PLC, which means any EU investor can take part in the future success of the venture.

name: Lift One
description: The Lift One project by Lifthium Energy, S.A., aims to establish a lithium refining plant in Portugal, contributing to the EU's capacity for lithium processing. By employing pioneering electrolysis technology primarily powered by renewable energy, the plant will transform lithium into battery-grade lithium hydroxide, essential for electric vehicle batteries. The integration of recycled materials, such as lithium from end-of-life batteries, emphasizes circular economy principles, reducing environmental impact and reliance on natural resource extraction.

name: Neves Corvo - 3RD SILO, LOMBADOR, Semblana
description: This project is an integrated extraction and processing project located in Portugal, consisting of mine extensions of the Neves Corvo mine, Semblana and Lombador North Phase 2, and a vertically integrated processing expansion, Yd Silo. The aim of the project is to develop two new copper orebodies to extend the Neves-Corvo mine life making use of existing mine infrastructure and processing facilities. Additionally, building a Yd ore silo will enhance underground materials handling management and copper and zinc production.

name: SALROM Baia de Fier
description: The SALROM Baia de Fier project is an extraction project, situated in the mineral-rich region of Baia de Fier in Romania. This project has the objective to re-open a historic mine and extract graphitebearing schists to produce high-quality graphite, using advanced techniques designed to minimize material losses and reduce environmental impact. The output of this extraction will be tailored for battery production, particularly for electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems.

name: Rovina
description: The Rovina project is a gold-copper extraction project located in Romania. The aim of this project is to produce high-grade copper concentrate from three Cu-Au porphyry style deposits in close proximity. The mining will take place over a period of 35 years from two open pits and one underground mine, with an estimated starting date in 2027.

name: Verde Magnesium
description: The Verde Magnesium project is an extraction project located in Romania. This project implies the extraction of magnesium ores by restarting mining activities from one of the world's biggest deposits of brucite ore. These ores will become feedstock for a magnesium smelter to be built, which is still to be further developed. As an extraction project, it sits at the foundation of the metallic magnesium value chain, providing a strategic raw material valuable across different EU industries. The business model adopts the principles of circular economy: clean technology to produce low-carbon magnesium, use waste streams generated by various industries in the magnesium production process, generation of low-carbon by-products to serve as raw materials for other industries.

name: MINA DOADE PROJECT
description: The Mina Doade Project is an extraction project in the Northwest of Spain, within the region of Galicia. The project addresses exploitation of pegmatite, a lithium bearing ore, through underground mining and a mineral processing plant for concentration. The project will use well-proven mining and beneficiation technologies to develop a small-scale underground mining operation, which will reduce dust and noise emissions as well as the impacts on the local ecosystem. The use of ore processing waste (tailings) to backfill underground mined cavities will significantly reduce the need for surface storage of mining waste and ore processing tailings.

name: LAS NAVAS
description: LAS NAVAS project is an extraction project close to Cåceres, Spain. It aims to extract lithium bearing minerals and to produce battery-grade lithium hydroxide in the long term. The lithium mineralization of the Las Navas deposit is primarily composed of spodumene, amblygonite, and lithium micas, mainly lepidolite and zinnwaldite. Other economically significant minerals present include cassiterite and columbo-tantalite. The technology needed to extract the ore, which is widely available and used in producing spodumene mines in Australia and Canada, would be made available by EU providers.

name: La Parrilla Mine (P6 Metals)
description: La Parrilla Mine project is an integrated tungsten extraction and processing project in southwest Spain. It is aimed at reopening an existing tungsten open pit mine connected to an already constructed processing plant. The mine is expected to be back in full production during 2026 with a life of mine of 18 years. The mine is situated on relatively flat ground with sufficient real-estate for all required infrastructure; existing plant, site offces, tailings ponds, access roads.

name: Mining project EL MOTO
description: El Moto tungsten project is an extraction project located in Abenåjar, province of Ciudad Real (Spain). It is a massive wolfram-gold porphyry deposit that will produce tungsten and gold, with bismuth and arsenic as potential by-products. The project promoter is a Spanish company with long experience in mining, civil works and renewable energy sectors. The project will be implemented sustainably in terms of monitoring, prevention and minimisation of environmental impacts.

name: Aguablanca Project
description: Aguablanca is an "Extraction Project" located in the Extremadura Region, Spain. The project is currently in the phase of restarting the operation by underground mining with a projected 6-years LOM to exploit strategic raw materials such as nickel, copper, cobalt, platinum group metals ("PGM"), gold and silver. Mined ore will be processed in the existing 5,000 tpd processing plant by three-stage crushing followed by conventional grinding and product slurry conditioning. Processing of the conditioned slurry product will be followed by a conventional sulfide flotation system to produce a bulk sulfide concentrate for the recovery of the above mentioned raw materials. All necessary permits required for the operating mine are in place and approved.

name: Polymetallic primary sulphite project PMR project
description: The Polymetallic primary sulphide project PMR is an integrated extraction and processing project in Spain. This project consists of an underground mine for the extraction of primary polymetallic ore and a hydrometallurgical plant, both located at the same site. Four metals will be produced, namely grade of cathodes of copper, zinc ingots, lead and, silver as metal cement product of high purity. The project promoter has developed an innovative and disruptive processing route for its polymetallic sulphide orebody, which will be the first industrial size commercial application and will significantly reduce its greenhouse gas footprint.

name: CirCular
description: CirCular is a recycling project located in Huelva, Spain. It is an innovative state of the art plant to recover non-ferrous metals such as copper, gold, silver, platinum, palladium and tin from waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) previously processed by authorized agents. The project is in the construction stage. Additionally, Atlantic Copper is currently developing feasibility studies to further increase the WEEE's processing capacity, to produce battery-grade nickel sulphate, and to recover precious metals. This initiative not only promotes responsible consumption but also minimizes waste and maximizes resource value, embodying the principles of the circular economy.

name: ReeMAP Project: Malmberget, Lulea Industrial Park, Per Geijer
description: The ReeMAP project is an extraction and processing project in Sweden. It aims at further expanding LKAB's businesses model by starting production of critical and strategical raw materials, as byproducts from the iron ore production. The project spans three key locations in northern Sweden. At Malmberget, mine tailings from the ongoing underground operation will be further processed to produce a concentrate containing rare earth elements. In Kiruna, the Per Geijer deposit, contributes substantial reserves of iron ore containing rare earth elements to the ReeMAP project. At the planned Luleå Industrial Park, the concentrates are refined into commercial products, including rare earth oxides.

name: Talga Natural Graphite ONE
description: The Talga Natural Graphite ONE Project is an extraction project located in Sweden. The project entails a greenfield development consisting of a natural graphite mine and concentrator The project will have natural graphite concentrate as an output, which can be used for further processing into natural graphite anode material. The project is particularly suitable for lithium-ion batteries, separating it from other graphite miners some of which are unsuitable for lithium-ion battery material.

Balakhivka Graphite Deposit
description: The Balakhivka Graphite Deposit project aims to extract 45,000 tonnes of graphite annually using open pit mining. The project is located in an industrial agglomeration in the Kirovohrad region in Central Ukraine with well-developed infrastructure and has a 20-year active mining licence with prolongation priority. The project promoter is an Ukrainian entitiy. The Environmental Impact Assessment report has been approved and relevant social and governmental policies are in place. The project is planning to at a later stage expand operations to a spheroidised battery-grade graphite (SPG) plant

name: CaledoNi project
description: CaledoNi is an industrial modernisation project with the objective of increasing the production of nickel with a better environmental impact. The project consists in developing a new dust extruction's line at Société Le Nickel's Doniambo pyrometallurgical plant, which will allow to increase production of nickel by minimum 640 t per year and enlarge metallurgical opportunities to diversify ore sources. Once commissioned, the Doniambo site is expected to reduce diffuse dust emissions by 30% and canalised dust emissions by 14%.

name: Integrated Dumont Nickel Project
description: The Integrated Dumont Nickel Project is a nickel and cobalt sulphide advanced stage development project located in the Abitibi region of Quebec, Canada. Construction for the project is expected to begin in 2026. Once in production, expected to be in the first quarter of 2029, Dumont will produce 42,000 tonnes of nickel annually which is sufficient for approximately 840,000 EV batteries yearly. The project has a planned life of mine of 29 years. The project was assessed as having a substantially lower carbon footprint compared to other producers.

name: Jadar
description: Jadar is an extraction project in Serbia. The project promoted by Rio Tinto via the local entity Rio Sava Exploration d.o.o. has the potential to contribute to the supply of lithium (battery grade) and boron (metallurgy grade). The Jadar Project would be developed as an underground mine and processing operation.

name: Kobaloni Energy Zambia Ltd
description: The Kobaloni Energy Zambia project is a processing project located in Zambia. The Kobaloni cobalt sulphate refinery is set to become the first of its kind on the African continent, producing batterygrade cobalt sulphate for pCAM manufacturing. The project will source power from hydro-power sources and process cobalt at the site of extraction. The project has already been designated as a Minerals Security Partnership project.

name: Maniry Graphite Mine Project
description: The Maniry Graphite Project in southwest Madagascar will extract and process battery grade graphite. The Maniry Project comprises the staged development of open pit mines, processing plant and associated infrastructure including water supply, power generation, accommodation village and tailings storage facility on an area of approximately 20 km2 and with a lifespan of 21 years. The Project Promoter is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange.

name: Greenland Graphite a/s and Norgraph a/s
description: GreenRoc Strategic Materials PLC is advancing a project to establish a vertically integrated operation for producing graphite Active Anode Material, intended for the European lithium-ion battery market. The initiative involves sourcing high-grade graphite in the Greenland Graphite extraction project from the Amitsoq deposit in southern Greenland and processing it in a facility near Arendal in Norway, the Norgraph processing project The Amitsoq site includes high-quality graphite resources and benefits from advantageous shipping logistics due to its accessible location.

name: Nussir
description: The Nussir project is an extraction project located in the north of Norwav It aims to extract copper from a proposed underground mine at the Nussir deposit, with mining conducted by long-hole open stoping. Work on planning processes, engineering and permitting has already started in 2009, and has successfully led to a zoning plan, tailings permit, and mining concession being granted. The expected production of this project is estimated by the project promoter at 15.000 tonnes of copper, which can be used for the production of high-grade copper concentrate.

name: São Miguel Paulista (SMP) Nickel and Cobalt Refinery Restart Project
description: The Säo Miguel Paulista Refinery Restart Project is a processing project located in Säo Paulo, Brazil. This project entails refurbishing and restarting operations at an existing "stand alone" plant with the aim to refine nickel and cobalt. These operations are estimated to cover around 3% of EU's annual nickel consumption and 4% of annual EU cobalt consumption. The refinery product will be specialised, high grade nickel and cobalt metal, which can be applied for the construction of highperformance alloys, plating, the chemical industry, and battery supplies.

name: Sarytogan Graphite Project
description: The Sarytogan Graphite Project, promoted by the company Sarytogan Graphite Limited, located in Central Kazakhstan's Karaganda Region and focuses on the extraction of the strategic raw material graphite. Graphite is crucial for advanced battery applications in electric vehicles, renewable energy storage systems. The mined ore is planned to be processed on-site, while parts of the production to be further processed to high purified graphite suitable for advanced battery application.

name: Songwe Hill Rare Earths
description: The Songwe Hill Rare Earths project is an extraction project, located in southeastern Malawi. This project focuses on producing a purified mixed rare earth carbonate (MREC) from the carbonatite-hosted deposit at Songwe Hill. This MREC will be utilised for the production of rare earth oxides, which can be used in the rare earth permanent magnet value chain. The project has undergone comprehensive feasibility studies and environmental assessments, culminating in a Mining Development Agreement with the Malawian government in July 2024.

name: Tungsten West
description: The Tungsten West project is an extraction project by Tungsten West PLC located near Plymouth in South Devon, United Kingdom. The project aims to restore the historic Hemerdon mining and mineral processing operations to produce concentrates of the strategic raw material tungsten. Tungsten is essential in strategic technologies due to its strength and durability, making it ideal for applications in the aerospace and defence sector. Drawing from established insights gained from previous mining operations, the project incorporates advanced mineral processing techniques to enhance efficiency and output.

name: Zandkopsdrift
description: The Zandkopsdrift project is an integrated extraction and processing project located in South Africa that will produce two Strategic Raw Materials magnet rare earths and battery grade manganese. The mining operations are fully permitted with sufficient reserves to support a 45year mine life. The production of two high value Strategic Raw Materials from a single integrated operation is expected to result in low production costs for both materials. A DFS is under way and scheduled for completion in 2027, with first production targeted for 2029.
